symptom: `mxcli test --local --db-type hsqldb` kept `deployment/data/database/hsqldb/<app>_test` between runs. Data a previous run committed (an after-startup seed, an `@cleanup none` test) was still there on the next run, so an idempotent init skipped seeding and tests failed on stale data. Measured on 11.12.2: a test asserting an empty table PASSed on run 1 and FAILed on run 2 after another test committed one row
cause: The file database is created by the runtime the first time it boots and opened as-is afterwards. `prepareLocalAppDatabase` had nothing to do for it, so nothing ever removed it; the `_test` suffix kept it off the dev loop's data but not off the previous test run's
file: `cmd/mxcli/docker/localapp.go` (`LocalAppOptions.FreshFileDB`, `removeFileDatabase` — refuses a name that is not one path element); `cmd/mxcli/testrunner/localapp_options.go` sets it for the file database
insight: Scope the reset to the caller whose database is its own scratch: the option lives on `LocalAppOptions` but only the test runner sets it, so `run --local --db-type hsqldb` (the developer's data) is untouched, and the test pins that the dev database beside the scratch one survives. The name is joined onto the deployment dir and removed recursively, so it is refused unless it is a single path element. Runtime control: same two-test file, main run 2 FAIL (count 1), fix both runs PASS. PostgreSQL's `<app>_test` database has the same carry-over (measured: run 2 FAIL) and is not reset by this change
